title: Savoring post-exposure pride to enhance the efficacy of exposure
summary: Fear of public speaking is widespread and can significantly impact everyday life. Exposure therapy – deliberately confronting the feared situation, in this case speaking in front of others – is a well-established treatment approach. This study investigates whether a brief, targeted exercise to enhance pride directly after exposure improves the effectiveness of exposure. Participants are encouraged to feel proud of having completed the exposure and to consciously experience and savor this feeling. To this end, people with fear of public speaking complete several exposure exercises in virtual reality (VR) across two exposure sessions, giving short speeches in front of a virtual audience. After both exposure sessions, one group receives the additional pride exercise, while the other group completes a comparison task that is neutral and unrelated to pride. Fear of public speaking and pride are assessed via questionnaire throughout the study, followed by an online questionnaire one week later. It is expected that the group receiving the pride exercise will report higher pride after exposure as well as lower fear of public speaking one week after the final exposure session. A total of 480 people with elevated fear of public speaking are planned to participate in the study. The study takes place across multiple universities and is coordinated by the University of Göttingen. Currently, 14 study sites are planning to participate.
conditions: Elevated fear of public speaking, PRCA-PS, Cut-off > 17, including both subclinical severity and clinical severity as a subtype of F40.1 Social Phobia.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Presence of fear of public speaking, confirmed by a PRCA-PS sum score in the online screening (cut-off > 17).
Exclusion criteria:
Previous participation in the same study; epilepsy or history of seizures (due to the virtual reality component).
